facts.fact: Industry analysis cited by Adwave (AI Digital) puts the typical average CTV CPM working range at $20-$40, with many campaigns settling near $25.
facts.quote: Industry analysis cited on this page (AI Digital) puts the working range around **$20-$40**, with many campaigns settling near **~$25**.

facts.fact: Premium CTV was often priced in a roughly $35-$50 CPM band from 2023 to early 2024, per the page's trend narrative.
facts.quote: **2023 to early 2024:** Premium CTV often priced in a **~$35-$50** band when ad-supported streaming inventory was tighter.

facts.fact: Mid-tier CTV averages moved toward roughly $25-$35 CPM from mid-2024 through 2025, per the page's trend narrative.
facts.quote: **Mid-2024 through 2025:** More ad tiers and FAST supply (Marketing Architects' "inventory glut" framing cited on the live page) pushed mid-tier averages toward roughly **~$25-$35**.

facts.fact: The page's 2026 planning outlook puts base CTV inventory around $20-$25 CPM, with premium targeting able to reach $40-$60.
facts.quote: **Heading into 2026 (planning outlook on-page):** Base inventory often planned around **~$20-$25**, with premium targeting and placement still able to command **~$40-$60**.

facts.fact: The page notes a seasonal CPM lift of roughly 20-40% during Q4 and peak demand versus quieter periods.
facts.quote: **Q4 and peak demand:** holiday competition; on-page planning note of roughly **20-40%** seasonal lift versus quieter periods.

facts.fact: The page notes prime evening dayparts often price roughly 30-50% higher than daytime.
facts.quote: **Prime dayparts:** evening TV windows often price higher than daytime (on-page note of roughly **30-50%** for prime versus daytime).

facts.fact: The page notes locking delivery to TV screens only can add roughly 15-25% to CPM.
facts.quote: **TV-screen-only device filters:** smart-TV inventory is scarcer than "any device streaming" (on-page note of roughly **15-25%** lift when you lock to TV screens).
